subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram DMs can still land in agent:main:main, polluting heartbeat/main session after #40519

question: Should this issue be split so the `heartbeat.session` precedence bug is fixed first, while Telegram DM default isolation remains a separate compatibility/product decision?
rationale: Source inspection shows a narrow heartbeat precedence bug, but changing Telegram DMs away from the documented `dmScope: main` default can break users who rely on shared main-session continuity.

options.title: Split heartbeat precedence first
options.body: Fix event-triggered heartbeat routing so configured `heartbeat.session` wins, while leaving Telegram DM defaults behind the existing `session.dmScope` behavior until separately approved.

options.title: Bundle Telegram DM isolation
options.body: Change Telegram private DMs to isolate by default in the same work, accepting the upgrade, docs, and regression-test burden for existing main-session users.

options.title: Defer to native per-session heartbeat design
options.body: Wait for the broader heartbeat-entry design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/60275, which may be cleaner but leaves the forced-session override path unresolved longer.

recommendation.title: Split heartbeat precedence first
recommendation.body: Fix event-triggered heartbeat routing so configured `heartbeat.session` wins, while leaving Telegram DM defaults behind the existing `session.dmScope` behavior until separately approved.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the clearest current follow-up owner from the adjacent merged event-routing fix and maintainer proof comment on the related closed issue.
